page: UpCloud PREMIUM-38xCPU-192GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 38 vCPUs and 38 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, this instance includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 5.05 GB of RAM per core. The CPU configuration utilizes a shared allocation model and features a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. Local storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong computational capabilities. In single-core stress-ng testing, the processor achieves top-tier performance within the top 10% of tested systems, while multi-core performance falls within the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier read speeds of 7289.98 GB/sec for small cached blocks, and strong uncached read and write speeds of 250.52 GB/sec and 107.36 GB/sec respectively for large blocks. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top 10%. Database operations perform exceptionally well, with PassMark database benchmarks scoring in the top 10% and Redis SET operations reaching 64.19 million operations per second.

The server offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for memory-intensive and database-driven workloads. While the shared CPU allocation presents a potential resource-sharing tradeoff compared to dedicated instances, the high core count and substantial memory density provide qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded applications. This configuration is appropriate for database hosting, static web serving, and moderate language model inference tasks, where its strong memory bandwidth and high database transaction throughput can be fully utilized.
